status: formal first version for development review; not yet frozen for bulk annotation
source: paired-view open coding of the development-only 48-trajectory discovery layer
unit: one atomic proposition; multiple propositions at different levels may coexist in a step
assignment_rules: Copy the smallest proposition supported by the visible pre-order record and retain the exact source text.
Assign type, level, and status to each proposition independently; do not assign one confidence value to a whole step.
A negative finding can challenge or exclude a proposition only when the relevant target was adequately assessed.
Nonvisualization, nondiagnostic examination, and not-assessed anatomy cannot by themselves produce excluded.
Observed constraints (for example pregnancy or renal function) are context unless the proposition explicitly concerns that constraint.
Use other for a clear recurring proposition outside this vocabulary and provide a proposed name; use unclear when the proposition or level cannot be separated without speculation.

status_definitions.suspected: Actively considered but not the leading or adequately established proposition.
status_definitions.likely: Leading supported proposition that still awaits decisive confirmation.
status_definitions.established: Adequately supported or explicitly known at this level; uncertainty at another level remains separate.
status_definitions.challenged: Still possible but materially weakened by valid negative, discordant, or temporal evidence.
status_definitions.excluded: Sufficiently and validly refuted for the current decision point.
status_definitions.unclear: Recoverable proposition whose status cannot be assigned without overstatement.

types.definition: A broad syndrome or incompletely localized process organizes the workup before one disease or finding identity dominates.
include: An intra-abdominal inflammatory or infectious process is present but its organ source is unknown.
The source of pain, sepsis, or obstruction remains unlocalized.
exclude: A named disease is the proposition being tested; use disease_or_finding_identity.
A known disease is being staged; use severity_extent_or_course.

source_examples.quote: makes gynecologic pathology (ovarian torsion, TOA, ovarian cyst) at least as likely as appendicitis

types.boundary_rule: A broad differential without a focal named proposition remains a frame; named competing propositions are coded separately when supported.

types.definition: The existence or identity of a named disease, lesion, collection, or observed abnormality organizes the workup.
include: A suspicious tubular structure represents appendicitis rather than another lesion.
exclude: Cause of an identified disease; use etiology_or_mechanism.
Extent or progression of an established process; use severity_extent_or_course.
types.boundary_rule: Do not collapse identity with etiology, severity, complication, or device status.

types.definition: A cause or mechanism of an established or strongly suspected disease/finding organizes the workup.
include: Duct dilation is due to a stone, stricture, or obstructing lesion.
exclude: A different organ system may explain the presentation; use alternative_source.
Device position or function; use intervention_or_device_state.

source_examples.quote: whether gallstones or biliary sludge are the precipitating cause

types.boundary_rule: Etiology is nested under the retained clinical frame; it is not an alternative source merely because it is another organ.

types.definition: Extent, grade, stability, progression, response, or resolution of a recognized process organizes the workup.
include: A collection has enlarged or responded to treatment.
exclude: A distinct adverse entity such as necrosis or perforation; also code complication.
Unidentified base disease; use disease_or_finding_identity or syndrome_or_source_frame.

source_examples.quote: fully characterize the extent of perforation or abscess

types.boundary_rule: Temporal qualifiers remain attributes; promote a new top-level complication only when a distinct adverse entity is proposed.

types.definition: A consequential adverse development of disease, procedure, or prior finding organizes the workup.
include: Perforation, abscess, necrosis, fistula, leak, hemorrhage, or superinfection.
exclude: Size or interval response without a distinct adverse entity; use severity_extent_or_course.
An unrelated competing diagnosis; use alternative_source.
types.boundary_rule: A post-procedural complication can coexist with intervention_or_device_state; do not force one to replace the other.

types.definition: A different disease, organ, or clinical frame may replace or materially compete with the focal explanation.
include: Gynecologic, urologic, vascular, malignant, or other bowel source may explain the presentation.
exclude: A cause nested under the retained disease; use etiology_or_mechanism.
An undifferentiated broad frame before any focal proposition; use syndrome_or_source_frame.
types.boundary_rule: Record which focal proposition the alternative competes with; a list alone is not evidence of equal probability.

types.definition: Position, patency, adequacy, effectiveness, or failure of a prior intervention or device organizes the next decision.
include: A stent or drain is positioned, patent, decompressing, or failing.
exclude: Leak, bleeding, infection, or injury caused by a procedure; also code complication.
Biological etiology independent of the intervention.

source_examples.quote: whether the ERCP stent is patent

types.boundary_rule: This type is only assigned when the intervention/device state is itself the proposition, not merely mentioned in history.

types.definition: A clear proposition recurs but is not represented by another type.
include: A supported novel proposition with a proposed type name.
exclude: A proposition that cannot be separated or supported; use unclear.
types.boundary_rule: Keep this residual open and review proposed names at every saturation round.

types.definition: The available text does not support a stable atomic proposition or level.
include: The order has several incompatible explanations that cannot be separated from available evidence.
exclude: A clear novel type; use other.
types.boundary_rule: Do not use unclear as a synonym for low clinical certainty when the proposition itself is clear.

conflict_cases.case: Established pancreatitis with suspected biliary cause

conflict_cases.decision: Identity may be likely or challenged, but nonvisualization alone cannot set excluded.

conflict_cases.case: Post-ERCP stent with possible bile leak
conflict_cases.decision: Code intervention_or_device_state and complication separately when both are supported.
